definitions.explanation: Two or more factors reinforcing one another so that their combined result exceeds the simple sum. Almost always used in compounds, above all {相乗効果|そうじょうこうか}.

examples.japanese: {二|ふた}つの{薬|くすり}で{相乗効果|そうじょうこうか}が{生|う}まれる。
examples.english: The two drugs produce a synergistic effect.

examples.japanese: {広告|こうこく}と{口|くち}コミが{相乗効果|そうじょうこうか}を{発揮|はっき}した。
examples.english: Advertising and word of mouth produced a synergistic effect.

examples.japanese: {二|ふた}つの{政策|せいさく}が{相乗|そうじょう}して{経済|けいざい}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The two policies worked synergistically to lift the economy.

notes:
Literally "mutual multiplication." Distinct from {相加|そうか} (mutual addition); a synergistic result is multiplicative rather than merely additive. Used almost exclusively inside compounds.

COMPOUNDS:
- {相乗効果|そうじょうこうか}: synergistic effect (by far the most common)
- {相乗作用|そうじょうさよう}: synergistic action
- {相乗的|そうじょうてき}: synergistic (used adjectivally)
